submitter: vigilant_designer_offer_analysis — H1c producer register gate: the offer-analyser mints banned-register lead_with points at 23-24% and the wash cannot win a race against the mint
rationale: The owner's copy rulings are enforced today only DOWNSTREAM of the analyst, on page copy, by rewrite_negations. The offer-analyser's own output — the ranked lead_with[] benefit points in site_specs.offer_ordering, which Decision C is about to wire into hero writers — passes through no register check at all. [MEASURED 2026-08-31] migration 667 repaired 41 banned-register points across the estate at 10:34:30Z. By 16:25Z the producer had minted 75 fresh points and 18 of them (24%) carried the same constructions; 15 are live across 8 sites, including RANK 1 on finetuning.uk (the site the owner rejected) and mortgagecalculator.co.uk. The live corpus moved 27% -> 13.5% on the wash and was refilling within the hour; all-history is 223/958 (23.3%). A previous session of this lane told the copy lane 'the corpus must be clean on both axes before fleet-wide wiring' and then RETRACTED it: that condition is true at an instant and false by the next regeneration. The gate is not a corpus state, it is a producer property. This matters more than a style tic because of the copy lane's own hardest-won finding — demonstrations govern, instructions do not — so wiring a 13.5%-dirty corpus in as writer input teaches the exact construction through the channel they measured as most effective. The owner gave the go-ahead for a producer gate (relayed via copy_quality_two_stage, 2026-08-31) and ruled REPAIR over fail-or-drop when the three modes were costed to him.

plan.risks: 1. The gate adds an LLM call on runs with violations (~16 offer-analyser runs/day fleet-wide as of 2026-08-31, ~a quarter carrying a violation). Bounded by max_tokens 2000 and one call per run, never per point. 2. Layer 4 (reject a prefix-of-the-original on differentiated points) is strict by design and will REFUSE repairs, keeping the original dirty text and recording it — that is the intended failure direction, but it means the gate's success rate on differentiated points is an open empirical question and MUST be read off the record rather than assumed. 3. The banned-word patterns are duplicated from a JSON file under docs/ rather than loaded, because docs/ is not in the image; the bidirectional lockstep test is what stops the copy is silently drifting, and it t.Fatal's rather than t.Skip's if the register moves. 4. The register's one blessed exception (idea.uk's report hero may say 'honest', decision record D-005) is deliberately NOT encoded in the scanner — a per-site exemption belongs to a caller that knows the site. offer_ordering is unserved rationale so no caller needs it today; a future caller on served copy must handle it. 5. This action is NOT wired by this change: the step is a _HOLD migration because a seed naming an unregistered action fails at runtime, so it is inert until the next roll.

edits.rationale: The register's banned_words arm, made readable from Go for the first time, plus the union scanner. Deliberately NOT a second home for the shapes: those stay in negationtells.go, which is their authority. Patterns are copied byte-identical from the JSON rather than loaded, because docs/ is not in the image and a runtime read would work on a workstation and fail in the cluster.

The lockstep, in BOTH directions: a register word with no Go rule is documented and unenforced; a Go rule with no register entry is a rule the owner never gave. Words are held to PATTERN equality, shapes to NAME equality only — the register's shape patterns are coarse documentation proxies (its own negative_reveal entry says so) and negationtells.go's are narrower and authoritative, so pattern equality there would force the careful regex down to the loose one. A missing register file is t.Fatal, never t.Skip: a skipped lockstep is one that silently stopped holding, which is the exact failure mode this file exists to prevent.

edits.rationale: The gate. Repairs rather than fails or drops, per the owner's ruling: FAIL leaves the site's previous (also dirty) ordering current so nothing gets cleaner and one tic costs a whole re-analysis; DROP throws away ~1 benefit in 4, some ranked first — verify_cited_cardinals drops a FALSE CLAIM, this would drop a real benefit wearing a tic. Never drops a point, never fails the step on a violation, and records every catch AND every refusal — what makes the producer's rate measurable is the record, not the refusal, and that rate is the only evidence any of this works.

judgeRegisterRewrite — extracted as a pure function so the half that decides what reaches the artefact is testable without a model. Four layers, failing closed. Layers 2 and 4 exist because measurement showed the shared judge cannot supply them, and layer 4 was found BY BEING WRONG: the three-layer version passed 667's actual leopardess repair.

registerRepairPrompt — carries NO rule text and NO examples of the banned constructions, which is load-bearing rather than terse. Prompt text demonstrating a form teaches it and scores as it; the register's own usage rule forbids pasting the patterns or their examples as prose into a model's window. The model is shown its own sentence and the exact fragment to remove, never a catalogue.
edits.sketch: asks for {"replacements":[{"index":N,"to":"..."}]}; per item prints the statement plus `remove this fragment: %q` (hits[0].Matched); adds a one-line marker on differentiated points that the distinguishing detail must survive; instructs 'Say what the thing IS. Do not replace the fragment with a different comparison.' A test scans the rendered INSTRUCTION half with the gate's own scanner and also fails if it names any shape.

edits.rationale: Every `from` string is a real live point copied out of site_specs with its site and rank — a fixture this lane COMPOSES exercises its own rule, because it is written by someone who already knows which arm should fire. Positive controls on layers 2, 3 and 4, so the suite cannot be satisfied by a gate that rejects everything. Each premise-check t.Fatal's if its case stops demonstrating what it was chosen for.
